title: Artificial Intelligence and Engagement Pricing in Accounting Firms: A Literature Review and Research Agenda
content: Accounting firms are adopting artificial intelligence (AI) quickly, but the way they plan and price engagements has changed much more slowly. This paper reviews research from four areas that rarely meet: the pricing of accounting and audit services, the productivity effects of AI on knowledge work, the use of AI in accounting and auditing, and activity-based costing and project control. The review finds that AI's effects on accounting work are large but uneven across tasks, that new review and oversight work appears alongside time savings, and that hours freed by AI are often absorbed by other work rather than appearing as lower recorded effort. Firm-level studies link AI investment to lower audit fees and to changes in staff mix, but almost no research examines how firms adjust the internal, hours-based plans on which fees are set. I identify six gaps: the measurement of activity-level AI effects, the cost of oversight, the fate of freed capacity, in-engagement monitoring, the sharing of AI gains with clients, and the position of small and mid-sized practices. I then propose a research agenda of seven questions with suggested methods and data. The paper aims to help researchers and practitioners study and manage AI-enabled engagements on the basis of evidence rather than general efficiency assumptions.
